svg.text: BrewPlans Auth — Google OAuth → Opaque Session Token
src/app/login/page.tsx → src/app/api/auth/route.ts → prisma.session → HTTP-only cookie → src/app/api/auth/me + logout/route.ts

g.text: Browser
login/page.tsx
Google Identity
accounts.id (GSI client lib)
/api/auth
route.ts (POST) — Vercel
Prisma
User / Session models
NeonDB
Session table (Postgres)
Protected routes
/api/auth/me, /api/recommendations, ...
1. Google OAuth Handshake (Google Identity Services, client-side)
google.accounts.id.initialize({'{'} client_id: NEXT_PUBLIC_GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID,
callback: handleCredentialResponse {'}'}) then .renderButton(...) — "Continue with Google" button rendered
User clicks button → Google's own popup/One-Tap flow authenticates the user directly with Google
callback fires: handleCredentialResponse(response) — response.credential is a Google-signed ID token (JWT)
Note: no separate authorization-code redirect — this is the GSI implicit ID-token flow
the ID token proves the user's Google identity to the browser; BrewPlans never talks to Google's servers itself
fetch POST /api/auth { '{' } body: { '{' } token: response.credential { '}' } { '}' }
2. Server decodes the Google JWT payload — decodeJwt(token) in route.ts
base64Url = token.split('.')[1] → Buffer.from(base64, 'base64').toString('utf-8') → JSON.parse(...)
extracts payload.email, payload.name, payload.picture
⚠ this is a raw base64 decode of the JWT payload — it does NOT verify Google's cryptographic signature
(no call to Google's tokeninfo/certs endpoint, no signature/audience/issuer check in this code path)
if payload or payload.email is missing → 400 "Invalid token"
3. Find-or-create User
prisma.user.findUnique({'{'} where: { '{' } email { '}' } { '}' })
if not found → prisma.user.create({'{'} email, name, picture, username: generateUniqueUsername(name) { '}' })
if found → conditionally updates picture (Google's latest wins) and backfills username if missing (pre-username accounts)
username collision-avoided via generateUniqueUsername() — deterministic slug + disambiguation suffix
note: no password is ever stored for Google-authenticated users — passwordHash stays null (separate quick-signup/quick-login flows exist for that)
daily login stat also upserted here (DailyUserStat.loginCount) — wrapped in try/catch so a stats failure never blocks login
4. Backend issues an OPAQUE UUID session token — NOT a JWT
sessionToken = crypto.randomUUID()
a cryptographically random v4 UUID — carries NO embedded claims,
no signature, no payload; it is a pure random lookup key
expiresAt = now + 30 days
prisma.session.create({'{'} data: { '{' } userId, token: sessionToken, expiresAt { '}' } { '}' })
INSERT INTO "Session" — row keyed by opaque token, FK userId → User.id (onDelete: Cascade)
5. Token returned to client as an HTTP-only, Secure cookie
response.cookies.set('brewplans_session', sessionToken, {'{'}
httpOnly: true, ← inaccessible to client-side JS (XSS-resistant)
secure: NODE_ENV === 'production', ← HTTPS-only in prod
sameSite: 'lax', expires: expiresAt (30d), path: '/' {'}'})
the cookie VALUE is the opaque UUID itself — nothing else is exposed to the browser
200 OK — Set-Cookie: brewplans_session=...; NextResponse.json({'{'} user { '}' })
6. Subsequent Requests — Session Lookup, NOT JWT Decode
example: GET /api/auth/me, or any Prisma-backed API route that reads the session cookie
Browser auto-attaches Cookie: brewplans_session=<uuid> on every same-origin request
route.ts handler (e.g. /api/auth/me GET)
const token = (await cookies()).get('brewplans_session')?.value
const session = await prisma.session.findUnique({'{'} where: {'{'} token {'}'},
include: {'{'} user: true {'}'} {'}'})
if (!session || session.expiresAt < new Date()) → 401 Unauthorized
expiry is checked in application code against the stored expiresAt column —
no cryptographic verification is possible or needed, since the token has no embedded claims
SELECT * FROM Session JOIN User
7. Revocation Path — POST /api/auth/logout
User clicks "Log out" → fetch POST /api/auth/logout
logout/route.ts
const token = (await cookies()).get('brewplans_session')?.value
if (token) await prisma.session.deleteMany({'{'} where: {'{'} token {'}'} {'}'})
cookieStore.delete('brewplans_session')
DELETE FROM "Session" WHERE token = $1 — server-side revocation, immediate
200 OK + Set-Cookie clears brewplans_session (Max-Age=0) client-side
key property: because the token is opaque and DB-backed, deleting the row immediately invalidates the session everywhere —
Key invariants (confirmed in code)
• Opaque token, not JWT: crypto.randomUUID() carries zero embedded claims — every "who is this?" question requires a DB round-trip (prisma.session.findUnique).
• No stateless validation is possible by design — this trades JWT's "verify locally, no DB hit" property for instant, unconditional revocation via a single DELETE.
• Session lifetime: 30 days from issuance (expiresAt), enforced by application-level comparison against `new Date()` on every lookup — not by cookie expiry alone.
• The Google ID token itself is decoded via raw base64, with NO signature/audience/issuer verification in this code path — the server trusts whatever email the
browser-received Google JWT claims. This is weaker than verifying against Google's public keys server-side.
• Session → User relation is onDelete: Cascade (per prisma/schema.prisma) — deleting a User row auto-removes all its Session rows.
• Cookie flags: httpOnly (blocks JS/XSS access), secure in production (HTTPS-only), sameSite=lax (CSRF-resistant for top-level navigation), path=/.
• Two more first-party auth routes exist (quick-signup/quick-login) that presumably follow the same Session-table + cookie pattern but with password-based
credential checks instead of a Google JWT — not shown here as they were out of scope for this diagram.
• Username backfill runs both at login (route.ts) and at session-check time (me/route.ts) — defensive double-check for accounts created before usernames existed.

Request / call
Response / return
